answer: Each identity buys one glacier expedition permit, locks 80 credits as bond, and files a falcon route log across the dune pass. Each entry carries one permit code, one per expedition, and the log records timestamps. An auditor verifies the code, checks timestamps against the route, and burns the bond for a missing or reused code. The k-th fee is 42+13(k-1); the 1,000th costs 13,029, and 1,000 fakes pay 6,535,500 plus 80,000 at risk. A rented-expedition ring fails: one code backs one route, and a copied timestamp flags both claims. An honest agent pays 42, bond back after a clean epoch.
